verdict.rationale: Omarchy's own docs show it is built for agent-driven operation. On first boot it invites you to set up a default agent and "put it to work on your computer", and it ships OpenCode and Claude Code preinstalled with launchers. It also bundles skills so you can "describe what you want" to build apps, plugins and themes, and lets you send your agent to a crash from the notification. The omarchy CLI is explicitly positioned for agents doing customization and configuration. missing for 10: a native natural-language interface (it relies on third-party agent harnesses that need sign-in), a documented scope of which system operations agents can reliably perform, and independent or hands-on corroboration of natural-language operation.
